label: late copy-phase steps (recall index >= 5, or final step of L=3 sequences), token-gated
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original input or at <DEL>), and only late in it: when outputting original token 5 or later (L>=6, mostly the last 1-3 outputs; 64% of mass at the final step, to_go==0) or at the final copy step of L=3 sequences (t=5, recall_idx 2), which holds the strongest activations (top examples are L=3, e.g. q b k <DEL> q [b]). Silent at recall indices 0-1 and 3-4, so it is essentially absent for L=4 and L=5. The position condition covers ~99% of activations and activation mass, but precision is only ~8%: within those positions, the identity of the current input token strongly modulates firing (h, m, 3, x, i, b have the highest rates; adding that token set raises precision to ~24% at the cost of recall to ~63%), and the remaining selectivity was not captured by simple token, repetition (in_count), or history variables.
